## What's new in v0.6.0

### The audit can bring its own provider and key

OpenCode 2.x relays model calls through its own inference gateway, which rejects an account credential (a PAT or an OAuth login). The background audit inherited that credential, so on 2.x it could fail with `HTTP 400 … Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint` — a credential-type rejection that no amount of retrying fixes.

`auditProvider` makes the audit POST to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint itself, with a key it reads itself:

```jsonc
"auditProvider": {
  "baseUrl": "https://api.deepseek.com",
  "apiKey": "{file:~/.secrets/opencode/deepseek-api-key}",
  "model": "deepseek-flash"
  // "headers": { ... }   // optional
}
```

- `apiKey` may be a literal, `{file:path}` (a leading `~` is expanded) or `{env:NAME}`. A reference that cannot be resolved fails the audit loudly instead of authenticating as nobody.
- `baseUrl` may or may not already end in `/chat/completions`; a query string such as `?api-version=...` is preserved.
- A provider that is present but incomplete is an **error**, not a silent fallback to the host credential — quietly working "fine" would hide that the option did nothing.
- With `auditProvider` set, no restricted `memory-audit` agent is registered: the plugin calls the endpoint directly.

Failures now name the fix. A rejected credential produces a hint that points at `auditProvider` (and at the actual endpoint and model being used), while a context overflow still suggests a lower `auditBatchChars`.

**Secrets stay out of logs.** Any key the plugin knows about is scrubbed to `***` before text is logged, persisted in `.memory/audit-state.json` (which is later injected into the model's system prompt), or thrown as an error — providers usually mask keys, but a proxy or a validation error may echo the whole value. The direct call keeps the host call's timeout and single-flight guard: while one request is unsettled, the next fails fast instead of stacking a second request on a slow provider.

### Install instructions are split by OpenCode version

OpenCode 2.x uses `plugins` (**plural**) with object entries; 1.x uses `plugin` (**singular**) with `[package, options]` tuples. One package registers both the `setup` and `server` hooks, but the config key and option shape differ, so the README now documents each version separately, including installs from a local directory.

### Docs

- `LICENSE` (MIT) added; `package.json` gains keywords, homepage, repository and bugs metadata.
- README rewritten: the bot's four outcomes (`promoted`, `recovered`, `skipped`, `failed`), `watch --interval` / `--dir`, the argument-less `memory_publish` tool, and the complete option list with examples.
- Landed just after the tag, and therefore on `main` rather than in this tag's tree: `README.zh-CN.md` (Simplified Chinese).

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0

### Install

```bash
opencode plugin add @chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory@latest   # OpenCode 2.x
npm i @chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory@0.6.0                  # manual
```

## What's new in v0.5.0

A small release with one idea behind it: **stop committing anything derived.**

### The index file is gone

Until now, `memory/_summary.md` was a committed index that CI regenerated on merge, and the injected prompt was built from it. That gave the store a second source of truth, and a workflow whose only job was keeping it in sync.

Both are deleted. Every session now derives the index directly from `memory/active/` at start:

```
[mem-D2oToptx] WebFetch 必须走 subagent，避免 context 膨胀
[mem-KP221qb2] OpenCode 2.x calls models through opencode.ai/inference…
```

Titles and IDs only, never bodies. Nothing is written to disk, so running OpenCode in a directory still does not create or modify a `memory/` folder there — and the index can no longer drift from what was merged, because it is computed from what was merged.

Consequences:

- The GitHub Actions workflow that regenerated the index is removed, along with the `[skip ci]` commit dance.
- `opencode-memory-bot regenerate` is kept as a **no-op** that prints an explanation, so older CI jobs that still call it fail nothing.
- Migration no longer writes an index at the end.

### The context budget is explicit

Only the index enters the system prompt, capped by `maxSummaryChars`. When the cap is hit, the model gets a subset plus a notice saying so, and can call `memory_read` for a specific body or `memory_review` to list the store. A growing store costs a growing index and nothing else.

### Housekeeping

- The committed `package-lock.json` is dropped from the repository.
- `AGENTS.md` and `DESIGN.md` updated for the derived index; the bot no longer knows about a summary file at all.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

## What's new in v0.4.0

### The model can publish its own proposals

`memory_publish` is a sixth tool: argument-less, and it runs the bot itself, so proposals no longer sit in staging waiting for someone to remember the CLI.

It needs no user confirmation because it only opens PRs — the merge is the gate — and all git work happens in a throwaway `git worktree`, so your checkout, branch and uncommitted files are never touched. Leftover worktrees from a crashed run are cleaned up on the next one. A lock file (`.memory/bot.lock`, atomic, with stale-lock recovery) keeps a `watch` daemon and `memory_publish` from running at the same time; when the lock is held, the call reports it and processes nothing.

To make that reachable, the system prompt now carries a one-line notice when proposals are pending, telling the model to publish. Same division of labour as everywhere else: the model publishes, the human merges.

### The bot survives interruptions

Each run reports four counters — **promoted**, **recovered**, **skipped**, **failed**:

- **recovered** — the branch was already on the remote (an earlier run pushed it and stopped before the PR). The bot finds that PR, or opens it, and clears the staged file. No second commit, no duplicate branch.
- **skipped** — nothing to do (target already retired, or a PR that cannot be opened); the staged file is left in place.
- **failed** — git or `gh` refused; the file stays for the next run.

Remote and default branch are now detected from `origin` (both `git@…` and `https://…` forms) instead of assuming `main`.

### The audit handles a store it cannot fit in one prompt

New `auditBatchChars` (default `400000`) caps how much memory text goes into one audit call. A larger store is split into batches, ordered so related entries land together and with a 3-entry overlap, and a memory is never cut in two. The default assumes a ~1M-token model at roughly one token per character (Chinese); lower it for a smaller context window.

An over-long prompt is now recognised as a context overflow and explained with a fix (lower `auditBatchChars`, or point the audit at a model with a bigger window) rather than surfacing as a raw provider error. `memory_review` also reports how the last audit went, including failures.

On OpenCode 2.x the audit call uses the host's stateless `experimental.generate.text` with an abort timeout, instead of depending on a session or agent existing.

### Everything else

- `maxSummaryChars` default raised from `2000` to `10000` — the index costs one line per memory, so a small store no longer truncates.
- `memory_propose` / `memory_update` / `memory_delete` now say plainly that a proposal is *staged only* and that no pull request exists until `memory_publish` runs.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

## What's new in v0.3.0

This release turns memory from "the model writes a file" into "a human merges a pull request". Almost every module is rewritten to make that gate real.

### One file per memory, status by folder

The single `MEMORY.md` with `MEM-NNN` counters is gone. Each memory is now its own Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, and the folder it lives in *is* its status:

```
.memory/staging/mem-*.md    machine-local drop folder, git-ignored, the agent writes here
memory/active/mem-*.md      merged truth; the only memories injected into context
memory/retired/mem-*.md     removed memories, with reason and provenance
```

Frontmatter carries the full lifecycle: `id`, `title`, `tags`, `author` (your git identity), `source`, `proposed_at` / `approved_at` / `approved_by`, `supersedes` / `superseded_by`, `retired_at` / `retired_reason`, `related_pr`, plus `intent` on staged files. IDs are random and collision-free (`mem-` + 8 base64url characters) instead of a counter, because several branches can now add memories at the same time.

### The bot, and the PR gate

`memory_add` becomes **`memory_propose`**: it writes a staging file and nothing else — it cannot touch `memory/active/`. A local bot turns staging into pull requests:

```bash
npx opencode-memory-bot once     # process staged proposals, then exit
npx opencode-memory-bot watch    # poll staging forever (default every 2s)
```

- `propose` → branch `memory/<id>`, commit the file into `memory/active/` (moving any `supersedes` targets to `memory/retired/` with a `superseded_by` link), push, open a PR, remove the staged file.
- `retire` → move the active file to `memory/retired/` with the reason, open a PR, remove the staged file.

Merge is the only approval. It is a local CLI rather than a GitHub Action because an Action runs remotely and can never see a git-ignored local staging folder.

### Migration from the old store

On first run the legacy `.opencode/memory/MEMORY.md` (and `.agents/memory/MEMORY.md`) — `Active`/`Archived` sections, `MEM-NNN`, `nextSeq` — is converted into one file per memory under `memory/active/` and `memory/retired/`. A `memory/.migration.json` sidecar maps old IDs to new ones so `superseded_by` links resolve. It is idempotent, keeps the legacy file as a backup, and never blocks startup.

### Proposals are scanned for secrets

`memory_propose` and `memory_update` scan title and body before writing. A credential-looking string (AWS key, GitHub token, OpenAI / Anthropic key, generic `api_key = …`) rejects the write with a message naming the **type** of secret, never the value — a memory is destined for a committed file, so a leaked key would end up in git history.

### The audit proposes instead of deciding

`review.json`, its dismissals and the `memory_review refresh` path are gone. The background audit now only produces **retirement proposals** in staging (with `superseded_by` for refinements), which the bot turns into PRs like any other suggestion. The PR is the durable record of a finding and its outcome; the audit never edits `memory/active/`.

Also changed: `auditIntervalMinutes` defaults to 1 (was 60), and the committed `memory/_summary.md` index — titles and IDs only, bodies loaded lazily through `memory_read` — is regenerated by a CI workflow on merge.

### Docs

`DESIGN.md` is added and `AGENTS.md` / `README.md` are rewritten around the PR-gated model: the agent holds no repository credentials and runs no git; nothing proposed is trusted before a human approves it.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory/compare/v0.2.1...v0.3.0

## What's new in v0.2.1

The first npm release of the 0.2.x line — and the first one that loads on either OpenCode generation.

### One package, two loaders

The default export is now `{ id, server, setup }`: OpenCode 1.x reads the `server` hook, 2.x reads `setup`, and the same tarball works under both. (`server` is deliberately not a named export, so the 1.x loader still sees exactly one plugin.) Configuration syntax did not change.

On 2.x the plugin adapts to the host's own registries rather than the 1.x hook shape: tools are added through the host's tool registry and the memory block through its context hook. The background audit uses the host's stateless text generation — no throwaway session, no audit agent to register — with a five-minute timeout.

### `auditModel`

New option (OpenCode 2.x): pin the model used by the background audit as `"providerID/modelID"`, e.g. `"bailian-payg/qwen3.7-plus"`. Without it the host default is used, which may be a model your account cannot call — region-blocked, or simply not enabled.

### Also in this release

- Tests now cover both loaders, so a change to one cannot silently break the other.
- README: npm badge, the "quit and restart after installing" requirement, and the npm plugin cache caveat — OpenCode may keep loading a cached copy of the package after an upgrade, in which case the cached folder must be removed and the app restarted.

Everything from `v0.2.0` — supersede links, `memory_review`, the model-judged background audit, `staleDays` / `backgroundAudit` / `auditIntervalMinutes` — reached npm for the first time here.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/chncaesar/opencode-plugin-memory/compare/v0.2.0...v0.2.1
